title: Towards True Speech-to-Speech Models Without Text Guidance
claim: Prior systems route speech through text intermediates, either cascaded or interleaved; ours understands and generates speech directly with no text bottleneck.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, each with bottom-to-top flow and a caption beneath
description: Three side-by-side vertical block diagrams compare spoken dialogue paradigms. Each flows bottom to top, from an input waveform to an output waveform. Panel (a), a cascaded pipeline, stacks ASR (purple trapezoid), Text LLM (blue box) and TTS (yellow trapezoid). Text strings sit between the stages: 'Hello! Who are you?' and 'I am a helpful assistant.' Panel (b), text-guided speech models, is wide. A Tokenize block (green) feeds audio tokens into a long Text-guided Speech LLM bar. The bar emits text fragments ('I am a', 'helpful assistant.') and audio tokens, linked by dotted loop arrows, and a Decoder (pink) produces the output waveform. Panel (c), true speech-to-speech models, is a clean stack: Tokenize, audio tokens, Speech LLM, audio tokens, Decoder. It has no text anywhere. The tangled dotted arrows in (b) draw the eye first, and the simple stack in (c) contrasts with them. Captions (a), (b), (c) sit below.
caption: Paradigms for spoken dialogue modeling. (a) Cascaded pipelines rely on ASR → LLM → TTS, discarding paralinguistic cues. (b) Text-guided speech models incorporate speech input but still depend on text as an intermediate during generation. (c) True speech-to-speech language models directly comprehend and produce speech, avoiding the text bottleneck.
abstract: Spoken dialogue systems often rely on cascaded pipelines that transcribe, process, and resynthesize speech. While effective, this design discards paralinguistic cues and limits expressivity. Recent end-to-end methods reduce latency and better preserve these cues, yet still rely on text intermediates, creating a fundamental bottleneck. We present MOSS-Speech, a true speech-to-speech large language model that directly understands and generates speech without relying on text guidance. Our approach combines a modality-based layer-splitting architecture with a frozen pre-training strategy, preserving the reasoning and knowledge of pretrained text LLMs while adding native speech capabilities. Experiments show that our model achieves state-of-the-art results in spoken question answering and delivers comparable speech-to-speech performance relative to existing text-guided systems, while still maintaining competitive text performance. By narrowing the gap between text-guided and direct speech generation, our work establishes a new paradigm for expressive and efficient end-to-end speech interaction.
